title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Alabama (Tuscaloosa Family Medicine Residency)
Department: College of Community Health Sciences, Tuscaloosa Family Medicine Residency
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Geriatric Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Founded in 2016, the University of Alabama Geriatrics Fellowship is dedicated to meeting the healthcare needs of older adults in the rural South and has trained five fellows since its first graduate in 2019.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: HonorHealth
Department: HonorHealth Academic Affairs (Scottsdale Family Medicine Residency faculty)
Start: July (off-cycle starts considered for applicants who missed the Match)
Eligibility: Graduates of family medicine or internal medicine residencies, including current residents and physicians already in practice
International applicants: Foreign medical graduates are considered; they must email a CV showing strong interest in geriatrics, ECFMG certification, proof of passing USMLE Steps 1-3 and summative evaluations of medical school and residency training
Application method: ERAS; participates in the NRMP Medical Specialties Matching Program (off-cycle applicants email the program's own application form)
Visa support: J-1 visa sponsored by ECFMG; HonorHealth does not sponsor H-1B visas (Canadian graduates must also use J-1)
Summary: HonorHealth's ACGME-accredited one-year geriatric medicine fellowship prepares family medicine and internal medicine physicians to be geriatric clinicians, educators, consultants and leaders using the Age-Friendly Health System 4Ms framework.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: HCA Florida North Florida Hospital (University of Central Florida College of Medicine)
Eligibility: Physicians trained in family medicine and/or internal medicine
Accreditation: Continued accreditation by the ACGME (ACGME ID 1251112033)
Application method: Through ERAS; NRMP code 1587125F0 listed on the programme page
Funding: Salary by PGY level: PGY-4 $69,014, PGY-5 $72,114, PGY-6 $75,358, PGY-7 $79,123 (plus $950 meals)
Summary: A community-based one-year fellowship at HCA Florida North Florida Hospital training family medicine and internal medicine physicians in clinical geriatrics and preparing them for board certification in geriatric medicine.

title: Geriatric Fellowship
inst: Full Circle Health (Boise)
Department: Full Circle Health Family Medicine Residency
Eligibility: Physicians who have completed three years of family medicine residency and are board certified or board eligible in family medicine
Summary: Full Circle Health's 12-month ACGME-accredited geriatric fellowship lets family medicine graduates work with board-certified geriatric faculty for a year focused on the clinical care of older adults.

title: Faculty Development Fellowship
inst: Full Circle Health (Boise)
Department: Full Circle Health Family Medicine Residency
Summary: A 12-month post-residency fellowship in Boise that trains fellows to become teachers of family medicine, working as outpatient clinic attendings and as hospital attendings on the inpatient medicine, obstetric and newborn services.

title: Primary Care Obstetrics Fellowship
inst: Full Circle Health (Boise)
Department: Full Circle Health Family Medicine Residency
Summary: A 12-month post-residency fellowship giving family physicians additional experience in operative obstetrics (caesarean and vaginal deliveries) and high-risk maternity care across the antepartum, intrapartum and postpartum periods, with continued family medicine exposure.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Missouri School of Medicine
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Eligibility: Board-certified physicians and residency graduates in family medicine and internal medicine meeting ACGME Section III eligibility; exceptionally qualified applicants considered as described in ACGME requirements; three letters of recommendation and USMLE or COMLEX scores required
International applicants: Applicants must hold a valid ECFMG certificate by January 1
Accreditation: Fully accredited by the ACGME (ACGME ID 1252821026); graduates meet requirements for the CAQ examination in Geriatric Medicine
Visa support: Applicants must obtain a visa before the programme start date (visa type not stated)
Licence requirement: Must be eligible for a Missouri medical license
Summary: A year-long ACGME-accredited fellowship at the University of Missouri training family and internal medicine graduates in patient-centred care for older adults across inpatient, outpatient, nursing home, hospice and home care settings.

title: Geriatrics Fellowship (Virtua Health / NJISA)
inst: Virtua Health / Rowan-Virtua School of Osteopathic Medicine (New Jersey Institute for Successful Aging)
Department: New Jersey Institute for Successful Aging (NJISA)
Eligibility: Physicians who have completed a residency in internal medicine, family medicine or psychiatry
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Geriatric Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Geriatrics fellowships offered through Virtua Health and taught by Rowan-Virtua NJISA faculty, combining clinical, research, teaching and health administration training in ambulatory, long-term care, PACE, hospice and specialty geriatric settings.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: Marshall University Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine
Department: Department of Family and Community Health
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Geriatric Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Marshall University's geriatric medicine fellowship trains specialty geriatricians for rural West Virginia and Central Appalachia, with emphasis on community-based research and serving rural communities.

title: Auburn Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Piedmont Columbus Regional (Midtown) / Edward Via College of Osteopathic Medicine - Auburn (VCOM-Auburn)
Accreditation: ACGME continuing accreditation (January 2025); ACGME program code 1270112145
Application method: ERAS only (listed on ERAS as Piedmont Columbus Regional (Midtown)); two-week audition rotations May-November for applicants
Summary: A one-year primary care sports medicine fellowship run with VCOM-Auburn, with training at Piedmont Columbus Regional (Midtown), Auburn University, Tuskegee University, the Hughston Clinic and local high schools, including osteopathic principles in athlete care.

title: Sports & Exercise Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) Heersink School of Medicine
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Duration: 2 years (with a Master of Science in Exercise and Nutrition)
Eligibility: Graduates of accredited residencies in family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, med-peds, physical medicine and rehabilitation, or emergency medicine
Summary: UAB's two-year ACGME-accredited sports and exercise medicine fellowship combines comprehensive sports medicine training (sports cardiology, ultrasound, concussion, exercise as medicine) with a Master of Science in Exercise and Nutrition.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS) Northwest Regional Campus
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: UAMS Northwest Arkansas sports medicine fellowship in which fellows help provide comprehensive care for more than 465 University of Arkansas Razorback student-athletes across 19 sports.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (Fontana)
inst: Kaiser Permanente Southern California - Fontana Medical Center
Deadline: 2 October 2026 (interviews September-November; slots may fill before the deadline)
Eligibility: Graduates of accredited residencies in family medicine, pediatrics, internal medicine, emergency medicine or PM&R
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: One of the first 20 accredited primary care sports medicine fellowships (1993), Kaiser Fontana's one-year programme combines sports medicine clinics, head team physician roles at high school, college and professional level, and primary care continuity.

title: Harbor-UCLA/Team to Win Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Harbor-UCLA Medical Center (Los Angeles County Department of Health Services)
Eligibility: Board eligible/certified applicants from family medicine, internal medicine, emergency medicine, pediatrics, and PM&R
Accreditation: Fully accredited fellowship leading to the Certificate of Added Qualification (established 2001)
Application method: ERAS application; participates in the NRMP; medical license and DEA required
Summary: Harbor-UCLA's family medicine residency hosts a fully accredited fourth-year sports medicine fellowship in which fellows serve as team physicians for local colleges, rugby clubs and a high school.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: MemorialCare Long Beach Medical Center (Long Beach Memorial Family Medicine)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Long Beach Memorial's primary care sports medicine fellowship combines continued primary care with focused experience at a Division 1 university, in the action sports industry and in the community, built around seven areas of concentration.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship Program
inst: AltaMed Health Services
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: AltaMed's sports medicine fellowship is based in a Federally Qualified Health Center, combining continuity and sports medicine clinics with protected didactics, MSK ultrasound training and care for underserved communities.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (Los Angeles Medical Center)
inst: Kaiser Permanente Southern California - Los Angeles Medical Center
Eligibility: Completed or completing residency in family medicine, internal medicine, emergency medicine, PM&R or pediatrics; board eligible or certified
Accreditation: Fully accredited by the ACGME; graduates eligible for the CAQ in Sports Medicine
Summary: Kaiser Permanente Los Angeles's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship centres on its sports medicine consultation clinic, with team physician duties for Cal State LA, local colleges and high schools and co-direction of the Ironman 70.3 California.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Eisenhower Health
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Application method: Participates in the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP)
Summary: Eisenhower Health's one-year primary care sports medicine fellowship for two residency-trained physicians offers team and mass-event coverage (including PGA, ATP, LPGA and WTA events), MSK ultrasound training and shared didactics with UC San Diego.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: UC San Diego Health
Department: Division of Family and Sports Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Training primary care sports medicine fellows since 1991, UC San Diego's comprehensive one-year programme produces CAQ-eligible sports medicine physicians across a variety of settings in the San Diego region.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of California, San Francisco (UCSF)
Eligibility: Family medicine residency trained only; minimum 3 letters of recommendation; signed AMSSM code of ethics
Application method: ERAS; virtual interviews for the 2027-2028 season
Summary: UCSF's ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship offers coverage of professional soccer, Cal NCAA Division I athletics, ballet, theatre, high school and adaptive sports, with robust ultrasound training.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Florida College of Medicine
Department: Department of Community Health and Family Medicine
Eligibility: Graduates of ACGME-accredited residencies; from 2027-28 three fellows annually, one each from family medicine, emergency medicine and PM&R
International applicants: The programme does not accept J-1 visa applicants at this time
Positions: 3 per year from 2027-28 (1 FM, 1 EM, 1 PM&R)
Visa support: Does not accept J-1 visa applicants at this time
Summary: The University of Florida's ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship (est. 2007) gives fellows abundant exposure to Gator athletics and North Florida teams and events, based at the UF Student Health Care Center and UF Orthopaedics and Sports Medicine Institute.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Northside Hospital Gwinnett
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Northside Gwinnett's non-operative sports medicine fellowship prepares primary care physicians for the CAQ in Sports Medicine with Georgia State University NCAA Division I coverage, PGA Tour, USA Rugby, Atlanta Ballet and high school athletics.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Hawai'i John A. Burns School of Medicine / Hawai'i Pacific Health
Department: Department of Family Medicine and Community Health
Eligibility: Board certified/board eligible physicians in family medicine, internal medicine and pediatrics
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited; completion leads to eligibility for the CAQ in Sports Medicine
Summary: The University of Hawai'i's 12-month ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship (est. 2002) makes the fellow part of the athletic care team for about 500 NCAA Division I student-athletes in 21 sports at UH Manoa.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Full Circle Health (Boise) / Idaho Sports Medicine Institute
Eligibility: Family medicine trained applicants only: completed (or completing) a 3-year ACGME-accredited family medicine residency and board certified in family medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Application method: ERAS only; ranked through the National Resident Matching Program; two letters of support, diploma, training certificates, state licences, USMLE/COMLEX transcript, CV and personal statement
Funding: Salary $82,873; $1,500 CME funds; support for AMSSM annual meeting and ultrasound course
Licence requirement: Unrestricted Idaho State Medical License and DEA required by the start of fellowship
Summary: A 12-month primary care sports medicine fellowship based at the Idaho Sports Medicine Institute and Full Circle Health, with work alongside Boise State University athletics, local physicians and a high school.

title: MacNeal Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Loyola Medicine MacNeal Hospital
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: One of the oldest primary care sports medicine fellowships, Loyola MacNeal has trained sports medicine physicians for over 30 years with clinical experience across the full spectrum of practice settings and athletic coverage.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Illinois College of Medicine at Chicago (UI Health)
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Eligibility: Family medicine, internal medicine, emergency medicine, pediatrics and med-peds residency graduates
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Application method: Participates in the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP); application review begins mid-August and is usually completed by end of August
Funding: Funded by the Department of Orthopedic Surgery; includes funding and support toward conference presentations
Summary: UIC's fellow-focused sports medicine fellowship, led by sports medicine physiatrists and based at the UIC Flames Athletic Center, covers NCAA Division I athletics, the Chicago Marathon and professional volleyball.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
Summary: Northwestern's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship immerses one fellow per year in non-operative care of athletes, split between the Evanston campus (over 500 NCAA Division I athletes) and Northwestern Memorial Hospital.

title: South Bend-Notre Dame Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Saint Joseph Health System / Beacon Health System / University of Notre Dame
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Since 1999 the South Bend-Notre Dame Sports Medicine Fellowship, a collaboration between Beacon Health System, St. Joseph Health System and the University of Notre Dame, has trained two primary care sports medicine fellows annually.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Iowa Health Care (Carver College of Medicine)
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Iowa's primary care sports medicine fellowship offers state-of-the-art ultrasound training and coverage of over 700 Division I athletes across 20 teams, professional athletes and a World Cup cycling race.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Kentucky College of Medicine
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: UK's primary care sports medicine fellows help care for more than 550 NCAA Division I athletes on 21 Kentucky Wildcat teams and serve as team physicians for Eastern Kentucky University, Kentucky State University, Georgetown College and local high schools.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: MaineHealth Maine Medical Center
Eligibility: Graduates of accredited programmes in family medicine, pediatrics, internal medicine and emergency medicine
Summary: MaineHealth Maine Medical Center's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship offers clinic, training room, team and sideline experience at area colleges, universities and high schools, with teaching of residents and Tufts medical students.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Boston Medical Center / Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine
Eligibility: Graduates of accredited programmes in family medicine, pediatrics, internal medicine and emergency medicine
Summary: Boston University's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship, based at the Ryan Center for Sports Medicine, covers BU varsity sports, Boston College football and MIT with extensive sports ultrasound experience.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (Providence)
inst: Henry Ford Providence Hospital
Summary: A community-based sports medicine fellowship running since 1997 in Detroit's northwest suburbs, taking one fellow per year with event coverage for Madonna University, area high schools and the Detroit Marathon.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Minnesota Medical School / North Memorial Health
Department: Department of Family Medicine and Community Health
Summary: Established in 1987 and one of the first of its kind, the University of Minnesota's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship has graduated more than 90 fellows and emphasises clinical practice, education, research and team coverage.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Missouri School of Medicine (MU Health Care)
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine (with PM&R and Orthopaedic Surgery)
Eligibility: Board-certified physicians and residency graduates in family medicine or physical medicine and rehabilitation
Accreditation: Fully accredited (ACGME ID 1272812108); graduates meet requirements for the CAQ in Sports Medicine
Summary: A one-year collaborative fellowship between Missouri's departments of family and community medicine, PM&R and orthopaedic surgery, with ultrasound in every clinic and team coverage of Mizzou SEC Division I athletics.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Medicine / University Health
Department: Department of Community and Family Medicine
Summary: The oldest active ACGME primary care sports medicine programme in Missouri, UMKC's one-year fellowship operates from the Orthopedic and Sports Medicine Center at University Health Lakewood Medical Center.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: SSM Health / Saint Louis University School of Medicine
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: The SSM Health/Saint Louis University primary care sports medicine fellowship trains physicians in return-to-play and interventional procedures, with sideline coverage at collegiate, high school and community levels.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Kirk Kerkorian School of Medicine at UNLV
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Summary: UNLV's ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship gives fellows Division I team coverage through the UNLV athletic department, whose head team physician directs the programme.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of New Mexico School of Medicine
International applicants: International medical graduates are welcome; a valid ECFMG certificate is required before a licence is issued by the New Mexico Medical Board
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Application method: ERAS; all positions offered through the National Resident Matching Program
Summary: UNM's primary care sports medicine fellows work as team physicians at high school and Division I (UNM Lobos) level alongside orthopaedic and PM&R sports fellows.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Albany Medical Center (Albany Med Health System)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Offering sports medicine fellowship training since 2010, Albany Med's office-based programme sees athletes of all ages from high school to Olympians and Paralympians, with a dedicated sports-concussion clinic and Ironman Lake Placid coverage.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (Boone)
inst: Mountain Area Health Education Center (MAHEC) Boone / AppOrtho
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: MAHEC's Boone sports medicine fellowship combines a high-volume AppOrtho clinic with team physician roles for Division I Appalachian State University athletics, local high schools, Lees-McRae University and regional clubs in the North Carolina mountains.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Medicine
Summary: UNC's ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship trains physicians from non-surgical specialties across academic, private and campus settings with teams from recreational to professional and international level and a robust MSK ultrasound curriculum.

title: Carolinas Medical Center Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Atrium Health Carolinas Medical Center (Wake Forest University School of Medicine, Charlotte)
Summary: Atrium Health's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship (28 graduates since 2005) offers high school, NCAA Division I and II and professional team experience (Carolina Panthers, Charlotte FC, Charlotte Knights) plus orthobiologics and concussion care.

title: Cabarrus Family Medicine Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Atrium Health Cabarrus
Department: Cabarrus Family Medicine Residency Program (Charlotte AHEC)
Summary: A one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship in which the fellow is head team physician at high school level and covers Division II (Catawba College) and Division I (Davidson College) sports.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: East Carolina University Brody School of Medicine / ECU Health Medical Center
Summary: ECU's unopposed sports medicine fellowship (accredited since 2001) offers extensive NCAA Division I team physician experience and a diagnostic and interventional musculoskeletal ultrasound curriculum.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Campbell University School of Osteopathic Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Application method: Apply via the programme; audition rotations can be requested
Summary: Campbell University's sports medicine fellows serve as team physicians for Campbell's NCAA Division I athletics, a high school football team and endurance events such as Ironman, triathlons and marathons.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Wake Forest University School of Medicine (Atrium Health Wake Forest Baptist)
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Wake Forest's primary care sports medicine fellowship trains fellows to be leaders, educators and skilled providers through teaching, research, event coverage and care of pre-adolescent to professional and recreational athletes.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Summa Health (Northeast Ohio Medical University)
Eligibility: Graduates of approved family medicine, internal medicine, emergency medicine, pediatrics, PM&R or internal medicine-pediatrics programmes; allopathic and osteopathic physicians accepted
Summary: Summa Health's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship, based in family medicine, takes two fellows a year and offers professional and high school sports coverage plus orthopaedic specialty rotations.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Summary: Ohio State's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship has fellows help care for more than 900 Division I athletes on 36 Buckeye teams, plus Capital University and local high schools, through six longitudinal block rotations.

title: Sports & Exercise Medicine Fellowship
inst: Cleveland Clinic (Fairview Hospital)
Department: Department of Family Medicine, Fairview Hospital / Cleveland Clinic Sports Medicine Center
Eligibility: Mostly family medicine graduates; allopathic and osteopathic graduates of internal medicine, pediatrics and PM&R residencies have also been accepted
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited; graduates eligible for the CAQ in Sports Medicine
Application method: ERAS; participates in the NRMP Subspecialty Match
Summary: Established in 1985 with 70 graduates, Cleveland Clinic's Sports and Exercise Medicine Fellowship is one of the oldest in the US, affiliated with family medicine at Fairview Hospital.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center
Department: Department of Family and Preventive Medicine
Application method: Participates in the NRMP Sports Medicine Match
Summary: OU's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship (since 1992) includes OU athletic training room and student health clinic work, small-college training rooms and monthly one-on-one MSK ultrasound training.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship (Tulsa)
inst: University of Oklahoma School of Community Medicine (Tulsa) / Advanced Orthopedics of Oklahoma
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Eligibility: Qualified physicians from family practice, pediatrics, internal medicine, emergency medicine and the US military
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: A one-year cooperative fellowship between OU-Tulsa family medicine and Advanced Orthopedics of Oklahoma, with team coverage of the Tulsa Drillers, University of Tulsa, Oral Roberts University and the Route 66 Marathon.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Lehigh Valley Health Network (Jefferson Health)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: LVHN's sports medicine fellowship offers independence with faculty backup, a personalised learning track, professional-sports and college training-room experience and a personal MSK ultrasound probe for the year.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship (Saint Vincent Hospital)
inst: Allegheny Health Network - Saint Vincent Hospital
Department: Saint Vincent Family Medicine Residency Program (AHN Medical Education Consortium)
Funding: Salary $79,248; up to $2,000 moving reimbursement; up to $3,000 for two national sports medicine meetings; 10 days PTO plus 10 days education leave
Summary: Saint Vincent Hospital's 12-month ACGME primary care sports medicine fellowship, sponsored by its family medicine residency within Allegheny Health Network, offers broad clinical experience for two fellows a year.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (Central Pa.)
inst: UPMC Harrisburg (UPMC in Central Pa.)
Deadline: Applications accepted 1 July - 1 September each year (virtual interviews mid-September to late November)
Eligibility: Residents from ACGME-accredited family medicine, internal medicine and emergency medicine residencies
Summary: A community-based sports medicine fellowship in Harrisburg with a hybrid longitudinal/block curriculum, high school team physician role and Dickinson College training room and football coverage.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Thomas Jefferson University (Sidney Kimmel Medical College)
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine, Division of Sports & Exercise Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited since 1996 (first in the Philadelphia region)
Summary: Jefferson's one-year sports medicine fellowship, ACGME-accredited since 1996, offers busy sports medicine/orthopaedics clinics, ultrasound training, research and professional, collegiate and high school sideline coverage with Rothman and Einstein Orthopedics.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: AnMed Health
Summary: A fully accredited one-year fellowship run with AnMed Orthopedics & Sports Medicine and Prisma Blue Ridge Orthopaedics, caring for large athletic populations in upstate South Carolina including Clemson and Anderson University.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship (Columbia)
inst: Prisma Health / University of South Carolina School of Medicine Columbia
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Prisma Health-USC Columbia's primary care sports medicine fellowship gives fellows high school, collegiate and professional sideline experience, fellow-led didactics and teaching of MSK ultrasound to community physicians.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Campbell Clinic / University of Tennessee Health Science Center (Memphis)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: The Campbell Clinic/UTHSC primary care sports medicine fellowship offers high-volume MSK ultrasound, orthobiologics and coverage of the Memphis Grizzlies, Memphis Redbirds, University of Memphis and performing arts, with eight CAQSM faculty.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Tennessee Health Science Center College of Medicine, Knoxville (UT Medical Center)
Summary: UTHSC Knoxville's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship provides professional, collegiate and high school athlete coverage under three CAQ-trained sports medicine faculty.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: JPS Health Network (John Peter Smith Hospital)
Eligibility: Primary board eligibility or certification in family medicine, emergency medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics or PM&R
Summary: Described as the largest primary care sports medicine fellowship in the US, JPS accepts all five specialty pathways and covers TCU, Texas Wesleyan, Nelson University, local high schools and boxing and cycling events.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Dell Medical School at The University of Texas at Austin
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Dell Med's primary care sports medicine fellowship, based at Ascension Seton Orthopedics South Austin, trains fellows in multidisciplinary, high-value care of physically active patients and team sporting events.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship (Texas Medical Center)
inst: Houston Methodist Hospital
Department: Department of Orthopedic Surgery (family medicine GME)
Summary: Houston Methodist's one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship gives access to elite athletes as official provider for the Houston Texans, Houston Astros and Rice University, plus performing arts medicine and a large school athletic trainer network.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship Program
inst: McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston
Department: Department of Family & Community Medicine (with Department of Orthopedic Surgery)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: A collaboration between McGovern Medical School's family and community medicine and orthopaedic surgery departments training sports medicine physicians to care for the whole person in a university setting.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Texas Institute for Graduate Medical Education and Research (TIGMER)
Summary: TIGMER's sports medicine fellowship, teaching primary care sports medicine fellows for over 25 years, has fellows act as team physicians for San Antonio FC, St. Mary's, Trinity and Texas A&M-San Antonio athletics and over 30 high school teams.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship (Sugar Land)
inst: Houston Methodist Sugar Land Hospital
Summary: Houston Methodist Sugar Land's newly accredited one-year primary care sports medicine fellowship includes concussion care, EMG exposure, ultrasound training, Rice University collegiate experience and Fort Bend ISD football sideline coverage.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: The University of Texas at Tyler School of Medicine (UT Health Science Center at Tyler)
Summary: UT Tyler's ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship, which welcomed its first two fellows in 2022, provides sideline coverage for UT Tyler Division II athletics, local high schools and community events in East Texas.

title: Virginia Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: HCA Healthcare LewisGale Hospital Montgomery / Edward Via College of Osteopathic Medicine (VCOM-Virginia)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: The LewisGale Montgomery/VCOM primary care sports medicine fellowship trains fellows across pediatric to professional and disabled athletes, applying osteopathic principles, with training in two NCAA Power Five conferences.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Virginia School of Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: UVA's primary care sports medicine fellowship builds each fellow's year around a personal 'Sports Medicine Bucket List' alongside UVA Division I, high school and middle school pre-participation, team physician and return-to-play experience.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Bon Secours St. Francis Medical Center (Virginia Commonwealth University-Bon Secours)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Bon Secours St. Francis's sports medicine fellowship offers rotations in primary care and orthopaedic sports medicine, VCU and Randolph-Macon athletics coverage, a high school assignment and the Richmond Marathon, leading to CAQSM eligibility.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Old Dominion University Macon & Joan Brock Virginia Health Sciences (formerly EVMS)
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Old Dominion University's (formerly EVMS) primary care sports medicine fellowship offers two primary care and two orthopaedic sports clinics, Division I football coverage, ultrasound training and experiences in pain medicine, adaptive sports and surf medicine.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (PM&R)
inst: UC Davis Health
Department: Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
Deadline: 15 September of the year before fellowship start (interviews virtual via Zoom; invitations mid-October via Thalamus)
Eligibility: Completion of PM&R residency; CV and three letters of recommendation (one from residency programme director)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited since 2009 (in the first cohort of PM&R sports programmes)
Application method: ERAS only; participates in the NRMP match
Funding: Salary equivalent to PGY-5 on the UC scale
Licence requirement: California licensure by the start of fellowship
Summary: UC Davis PM&R's one-year sports medicine fellowship, ACGME-accredited since 2009, trains physiatrists in sports and musculoskeletal medicine with sports-board-certified physiatrists, orthopaedic surgeons and Sacramento River Cats team physicians.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (PM&R)
inst: Montefiore Einstein (Montefiore Medical Center / Albert Einstein College of Medicine)
Summary: Montefiore Einstein's one-year ACGME-accredited PM&R sports medicine fellowship (est. 2014) provides comprehensive musculoskeletal and concussion care across Montefiore, Jacobi, North Central Bronx and St. John's Riverside, with NYCFC and Division III college coverage.

title: Spine and Sports Medicine Fellowship (ACGME Sports Medicine positions)
inst: Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS)
Application method: ACGME sports positions obtained through the Match
Funding: Stipend $99,585.34 per annum with benefits; subsidised housing available
Summary: HSS's physiatry Spine and Sports Medicine Fellowship trains future leaders in nonsurgical musculoskeletal care and interventional physiatry, with St. John's University, New York Red Bulls, Long Island Nets and Juilliard coverage for sports fellows.

title: Interventional Spine and Musculoskeletal Medicine (ISMM) Fellowship
inst: Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS)
Accreditation: NASS-recognised Interventional Spine and Musculoskeletal Medicine position (not ACGME-accredited)
Application method: SF Match; successful applicants must withdraw from other matches such as ACGME Sports or Pain
Funding: Stipend $99,585.34 per annum with benefits; subsidised housing available
Summary: The NASS-recognised ISMM position within HSS's Spine and Sports Medicine Fellowship trains physiatrists in fluoroscopic and ultrasound-guided spine and musculoskeletal procedures, electrodiagnostics and nonsurgical musculoskeletal care.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (Rusk Rehabilitation)
inst: NYU Langone Health (Rusk Rehabilitation, NYU Grossman School of Medicine)
Summary: NYU Langone Rusk Rehabilitation's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship offers multidisciplinary training with physiatry and orthopaedic sports specialists, musculoskeletal ultrasound teaching and performing arts medicine electives.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: UT Southwestern Medical Center
Summary: UT Southwestern's one-year accredited brain injury medicine fellowship emphasises post-acute brain injury management, with acute care at Parkland (Texas's first Level I trauma centre) and research through the North Texas TBI Model System.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: UT Southwestern Medical Center / Children's Health
Summary: UT Southwestern and Children's Health offer one- and two-year ACGME-accredited pediatric rehabilitation medicine fellowships covering TBI, multiple trauma, SCI (including acute ICU care), inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation and research.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (PM&R)
inst: UT Southwestern Medical Center
Summary: UT Southwestern PM&R's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship provides training in primary care sports medicine, MSK ultrasound, procedures, concussion management and athletic event coverage.

title: Interventional Spine and Musculoskeletal Medicine Fellowship
inst: UT Southwestern Medical Center
Department: Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
Summary: UT Southwestern's one-year ISMM fellowship gives board-eligible/certified physicians multidisciplinary spine and musculoskeletal training with PM&R, anaesthesiology pain, spine surgery, radiology, therapy and psychology faculty.

title: Spasticity Management Fellowship
inst: UT Southwestern Medical Center
Summary: UT Southwestern's one-year spasticity management fellowship trains fellows to evaluate and treat spasticity in adults and children, including chemodenervation, chemoneurolysis, diagnostic motor nerve blocks and intrathecal pump management.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Medical College of Wisconsin
Department: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery (PM&R sports medicine)
Summary: MCW's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship has CAQ faculty from PM&R, FM, pediatrics and EM, with pediatric and adult sports clinics, adaptive sports, a multidisciplinary concussion programme and AMSSM-guided ultrasound training.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: Rady Children's Hospital San Diego / University of California, Irvine
Summary: The Rady Children's/UC Irvine two-year ACGME-accredited pediatric rehabilitation medicine fellowship trains physiatrists across inpatient rehabilitation, multidisciplinary clinics, neonatal consultation, tone management, electrodiagnostics and motion analysis.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: Indiana University School of Medicine / Riley Hospital for Children
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: IU's pediatric rehabilitation medicine fellowship trains academic clinicians to care for children with chronic conditions and disabilities, with rotations on Riley Hospital for Children's 10-bed inpatient rehabilitation unit.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: Kennedy Krieger Institute / Johns Hopkins University
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: The Kennedy Krieger/Johns Hopkins PRM fellowship trains clinicians across the pediatric rehabilitation continuum, from Johns Hopkins consults and PICU to Kennedy Krieger inpatient, outpatient and day-hospital programmes.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Minnesota Medical School / Gillette Children's Specialty Healthcare
Eligibility: Graduates of an accredited PM&R residency or combined pediatrics-PM&R residency
Summary: Offered with Gillette Children's, the University of Minnesota PRM fellowship trains academic pediatric physiatrists in cerebral palsy, spinal dysraphism, SCI, acquired brain injury, limb deficiency and neuromuscular disease.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: Children's Mercy Kansas City / University of Kansas Medical Center
Funding: 2026-27 salaries: PGY-4 $83,720; PGY-5 $84,657.60; PGY-6 $86,841.60; PGY-7 $90,043.20; PGY-8 $92,310.40; $1,500 educational and $2,250 professional stipends; premium-free health and dental
Summary: Children's Mercy's two-year ACGME-accredited PRM fellowship develops pediatric physiatrists through broad outpatient, inpatient and consultation experience, with individualised education and specialised training in all major areas of pediatric physiatry.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: Montefiore Einstein (Montefiore Medical Center / Albert Einstein College of Medicine)
Eligibility: Board certified or board-eligible candidates trained in PM&R
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited; fellows may become eligible for PRM subspecialty boards
Summary: Montefiore Einstein's two-year ACGME-accredited PRM fellowship covers congenital and acquired childhood disabilities with outpatient clinics at Montefiore and the Rose F. Kennedy Center, inpatient rehabilitation at Blythedale Children's Hospital and spasticity procedures.

title: Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship (Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine)
inst: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center
Duration: 1 or 2 years depending on prior training
Summary: Cincinnati Children's ACGME-accredited rehabilitation medicine fellowship offers one- and two-year tracks with a 12-bed CARF-accredited inpatient unit, multidisciplinary clinics and procedural training in EMG/NCS and neurolysis.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: Nationwide Children's Hospital / The Ohio State University
Department: Section of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
Eligibility: Completion of a four-year ACGME-accredited PM&R residency or five-year combined pediatrics-PM&R programme; board eligible or certified in PM&R
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Nationwide Children's PRM fellowship, the pediatric branch of Ohio State PM&R, meets ABPMR training requirements for PRM certification, with over 130 inpatient admissions a year, intrathecal baclofen management and specialty clinics.

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation Medicine Fellowship
inst: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP)
Summary: CHOP's new two-year PRM fellowship (two ACGME-accredited positions per year) trains educators and clinicians to treat children with acute and chronic functional deficits and to improve quality of care.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Kentucky College of Medicine (Cardinal Hill Rehabilitation Hospital)
Application method: Accepted through the National Resident Matching Program
Summary: Kentucky's one-year ACGME-accredited brain injury medicine fellowship is housed at the 232-bed Cardinal Hill Rehabilitation Hospital and prepares fellows for the ABPMR Brain Injury Medicine subspecialty examination.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center
Application method: Letter of interest to the programme (see application timeline)
Summary: Ohio State PM&R's new one-year ACGME-accredited brain injury medicine fellowship rotates through Wexner Medical Center and Nationwide Children's, including a disorders of consciousness programme and the Ohio Regional TBI Model System.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Arizona College of Medicine - Tucson
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Eligibility: Fellows trained in family medicine, internal medicine and emergency medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Founded in 2004, Arizona's one-year primary care sports medicine fellowship covers Big 12 Wildcat athletics, adaptive athletics, AHL hockey, USA Rugby, professional rodeo and El Tour de Tucson, with diagnostic ultrasound training.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Indiana University School of Medicine
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: IU's one-year primary care sports medicine fellowship alternates between sports medicine faculty and orthopaedists, preparing fellows for the CAQ in Sports Medicine with ultrasound, PRP, concussion and mass event coverage experience.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: NYU Langone Health (Rusk Rehabilitation, NYU Grossman School of Medicine)
Summary: NYU Langone Rusk Rehabilitation's one-year ACGME-accredited brain injury medicine fellowship trains fellows on inpatient units at NYU Langone Orthopedic Hospital, Kimmel Pavilion, Tisch and Bellevue plus outpatient brain injury services.

title: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Sports Medicine Fellowship (Non-operative)
inst: Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis (WashU Medicine Orthopedics)
Application method: Primary care sports medicine match; interviews October-November, rank list mid-December
Summary: WashU's ACGME-accredited non-operative PM&R sports medicine fellowship, housed in orthopaedic surgery, offers an Orthopedic Injury Clinic, fellow-run clinic, ultrasound and fluoroscopic procedures and complex nerve injury experience.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of California, Irvine (UCI Health)
Summary: UCI's ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship combines primary care and orthopaedic sports medicine (including an FQHC sports clinic) with NCAA Division I, X-Games, AVP and Ironman 70.3 Oceanside event coverage and extensive ultrasound training.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Henry Ford Hospital (Henry Ford Health)
Eligibility: Family medicine, emergency medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, med-peds and PM&R
Application method: Applications reviewed July/August; 3-4 interview dates (virtual/in person) in October/November
Summary: Henry Ford's one-year ACGME primary care sports medicine fellowship, based at the Henry Ford Center for Athletic Medicine/Detroit Pistons Performance Center, serves the Lions, Tigers, Pistons and Red Wings plus local schools and colleges.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Advocate Lutheran General Hospital
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Positions: Two fellows (one full-time, one part-time) noted in the clinic team
Summary: One of the oldest primary care sports medicine fellowships in the US, Advocate Lutheran General trains fellows in complete athlete management with University of Illinois Division I training room and sideline work and a human performance lab.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship (Asheville)
inst: Mountain Area Health Education Center (MAHEC)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: MAHEC's Asheville primary care sports medicine fellowship emphasises mentorship, scholarship and teaching, with training in lifestyle medicine, ultrasound, running medicine, gait analysis, female athlete care and team physician work.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: ChristianaCare
Eligibility: Graduates of ACGME-accredited allopathic or osteopathic programmes in family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, emergency medicine or PM&R
Summary: ChristianaCare's fully accredited one-year primary care sports medicine fellowship (since 2007) offers University of Delaware and high school coverage plus sports cardiology, exercise physiology and cadaveric anatomy exposure.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: Corewell Health Taylor Hospital
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Brain Injury Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: Corewell Health Taylor's brain injury medicine fellowship trains physicians in a 14-bed neurotrauma rehabilitation unit plus consultation, concussion and follow-up clinics, including baclofen pump management and chemodenervation.

title: Geriatric Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Louisville School of Medicine
Department: Department of Family and Geriatric Medicine (Trager Institute)
Eligibility: Physicians who have completed a residency in family medicine or internal medicine
Application method: ERAS with 3-5 letters of recommendation; applications screened before interview invitations
Funding: PGY-4 stipend $71,322.28 per year (as of July 2026)
Summary: Louisville's one-year ACGME-accredited geriatric fellowship, affiliated with the Trager Institute, trains fellows across UofL Hospital, Jewish Hospital, Frazier Rehab, the VA, PACE and home care.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Baptist Health South Florida / Florida International University (FIU) Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine
Summary: The FIU/Baptist Health one-year primary care sports medicine fellowship, based at Baptist Health Orthopedic Institute, offers year-round high school, collegiate and professional team coverage alongside team physicians and athletic trainers.

title: Cancer Rehabilitation Fellowship
inst: Baptist Health South Florida (Herbert Wertheim Cancer Institute)
Summary: Baptist Health's cancer rehabilitation fellowship at the Herbert Wertheim Cancer Institute trains physiatrists in holistic, multidisciplinary assessment and treatment of physical impairments before, during and after cancer treatment, including ultrasound-guided and spinal procedures.

title: Rural Medicine Fellowship
inst: Full Circle Health (Boise)
Department: Full Circle Health Family Medicine Residency
Start: Approximately the last week of July
Deadline: 11 September 2026 (virtual interviews 7 and 13 October; position offered by 16 October 2026)
Eligibility: Completed a 3-year ACGME-accredited family medicine residency and board certified in family medicine; CV, personal statement, programme director letter, two further references and procedure/ultrasound numbers
Application method: Email application to the fellowship coordinator
Funding: Salary $82,873; $1,500 CME funds; ATLS time and funding; Butterfly ultrasound provided
Visa support: Not able to sponsor visas for the fellowship at this time
Summary: Full Circle Health's rural medicine fellowship trains broad-spectrum family physicians in acute care, trauma, critical care, EMS and procedures for practice in rural, underserved or isolated communities.

title: Addiction Medicine Fellowship
inst: Marshall University Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine
Department: Division of Addiction Sciences, Department of Family and Community Health
Eligibility: Completion of a residency in family medicine
Summary: Marshall's one-year addiction medicine fellowship lets family physicians pursue ABPM board certification while joining Huntington's comprehensive response to addiction in Appalachia, with inpatient and outpatient experience and research.

title: Family Medicine Faculty Development Fellowship
inst: University of Rochester Medical Center (URMC)
Eligibility: Board certified or board eligible family physicians eligible for a New York State licence
Licence requirement: Eligible to obtain a New York State physician licence
Summary: URMC's family medicine faculty development fellowship, with over 20 years' experience, prepares fellows for academic careers serving underserved populations, with optional tracks in health services research, medical education or family therapy.

title: Maternal Child Health Fellowship
inst: University of Rochester Medical Center (URMC) / Highland Hospital

Eligibility: Board certified or board eligible family physicians eligible for a New York State licence
Positions: 4 per year (2 surgically focused track, 2 advanced obstetrics track)
Funding: PGY-4 salary for 2027-28; CME $2,100/year plus $2,000 for rural conferences; 22 days vacation; housing provided in Wellsville
Licence requirement: Eligible to obtain a New York State physician licence
Summary: URMC's one-year maternal child health fellowship for family physicians offers surgically focused and advanced obstetrics tracks with high-volume obstetrics at Highland Hospital and rural maternity immersion in Wellsville, NY.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Rochester Medical Center (URMC) / Highland Family Medicine
Eligibility: Board certified or board eligible family physicians eligible for a New York State licence
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Licence requirement: Eligible to obtain a New York State physician licence
Summary: URMC's primary care sports medicine fellowship trains academic sports physicians through Highland Family Medicine consultation, orthopaedic and spine rotations, POCUS training and team coverage for St. John Fisher University and Penfield High School.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: United Health Services (UHS) Hospitals
Summary: UHS's twelve-month ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship features a longitudinal MSK ultrasound curriculum and coverage of Binghamton University Division I teams, the Binghamton Black Bears, SUNY Broome and the Dick's Sporting Goods Open.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Conway Medical Center
Eligibility: Graduates of family medicine, internal medicine or emergency medicine residencies
Summary: Conway Medical Center's one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship offers Coastal Carolina University Division I coverage, surfing, combat sports and AVP sand volleyball events, plus orthobiologics (PRP, BMAC) and ultrasound training.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Lake Erie College of Osteopathic Medicine (LECOM)
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited (Sports Medicine, Family Medicine) (per AAMC ERAS participating-programs list)
Summary: LECOM's sports medicine fellowship develops osteopathic sports physicians with extensive musculoskeletal ultrasound, osteopathic manipulative treatment and bio-regenerative injection training plus high school and collegiate team physician experience.

title: Sports Medicine (Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation) Fellowship
inst: MedStar National Rehabilitation Hospital / Georgetown University School of Medicine
Summary: The MedStar Georgetown/NRH one-year ACGME-accredited PM&R sports medicine fellowship offers multidisciplinary musculoskeletal training, diagnostic and interventional ultrasound, fluoroscopic spine procedures and the National Capital Sports Medicine Consortium didactics.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: MedStar National Rehabilitation Hospital / Georgetown University School of Medicine
Application method: Participates in the National Brain Injury Match (NRMP Rehabilitation Medicine Match, per the programme page)
Summary: MedStar NRH's ACGME-accredited brain injury medicine fellowship offers one-year clinical and two-year clinical-research tracks across acute care, inpatient rehabilitation and post-acute settings, with civilian and military colleagues.

title: Brain Injury Fellowship
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (The Mount Sinai Hospital)
Department: Department of Rehabilitation and Human Performance
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited residency in PM&R, neurology or psychiatry
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited; prepares fellows for the ABPMR Brain Injury Medicine examination
Funding: Salary $101,250; $2,000 education stipend; travel and meal stipends; 20 vacation days
Summary: Mount Sinai's one-year ACGME-accredited brain injury fellowship, at a TBI Model Systems centre, trains fellows across inpatient and outpatient programmes including disorders of consciousness and ultrasound-guided spasticity management.

title: Spinal Cord Injury Fellowship
inst: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (The Mount Sinai Hospital)
Department: Department of Rehabilitation and Human Performance
Eligibility: Completion of an ACGME-accredited residency in PM&R, family medicine, neurology, internal medicine, anesthesiology, emergency medicine, neurosurgery, orthopaedic surgery, pediatrics, surgery, urology or plastic surgery
Accreditation: Not stated on official page (programme within Mount Sinai's CARF-accredited SCI Rehabilitation Program)
Application method: Participates in the National Resident Matching Program; application form via the Academy of Spinal Cord Injury Professionals, submitted to the fellowship coordinator
Summary: Mount Sinai's one-year SCI fellowship rotates through The Mount Sinai Hospital, Mount Sinai Morningside and the James J. Peters VA, including specialty clinics and a home visit programme for veterans with spinal cord injury.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: Burke Rehabilitation Hospital (Montefiore Health System / Albert Einstein College of Medicine)
Eligibility: Board eligible/board certified physiatrists and/or neurologists
Summary: Burke Rehabilitation's one-year ACGME-accredited brain injury medicine fellowship trains two physiatrists or neurologists across the spectrum of brain injury rehabilitation, with on-campus housing when available.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Burke Rehabilitation Hospital (Montefiore Health System)
Summary: Burke Rehabilitation's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship for two physicians includes outpatient sports and musculoskeletal care, concussion care, orthopaedics, MSK radiology and high school, college and professional soccer coverage.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship - Riverside Methodist Hospital
inst: OhioHealth Riverside Methodist Hospital
Eligibility: Physicians from family medicine, internal medicine, pediatrics, PM&R and emergency medicine
Application method: NRMP programme code 1567127F0 (stated on programme page)
Summary: OhioHealth Riverside Methodist's one-year ACGME-accredited sports medicine fellowship uses four three-month rotations across up to 10 practice sites with in-office ultrasound, radiology and physical therapy.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute (Hackensack Meridian Health)
Department: Center for Brain Injuries; Department of PM&R, Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine and Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School
Summary: JFK Johnson's one-year ACGME-accredited brain injury medicine fellowship exposes a physiatrist to the full continuum of acquired brain injury care, from acute trauma consults to inpatient, sub-acute and outpatient rehabilitation and disorders of consciousness.

title: Pain Medicine Fellowship
inst: JFK Johnson Rehabilitation Institute (Hackensack Meridian Health)
Summary: JFK Johnson's one-year ACGME-accredited multidisciplinary pain medicine fellowship, based in rehabilitation medicine, trains fellows in fluoroscopic spinal interventions, spinal cord stimulators, ultrasound-guided blocks, regenerative techniques and pain psychology.

title: Brain Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston / TIRR Memorial Hermann
Summary: UTHealth Houston's one-year ACGME-accredited brain injury medicine fellowship, run with Baylor College of Medicine PM&R, trains physiatrists at TIRR Memorial Hermann and Memorial Hermann-TMC with extensive spasticity and intrathecal baclofen training.

title: Spinal Cord Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston / TIRR Memorial Hermann / Michael E. DeBakey VA Medical Center
Summary: UTHealth Houston's ACGME-accredited SCI medicine fellowship splits training between TIRR Memorial Hermann/Memorial Hermann-TMC and the Michael E. DeBakey VA SCI Service Line, balancing acute and chronic SCI care.

title: Spasticity and Neurorehabilitation Fellowship
inst: McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston
Summary: UTHealth Houston's non-ACGME spasticity fellowship trains future leaders in spasticity management, including neurotoxin chemodenervation, phenol/alcohol neurolysis, cryoneurolysis, needle fasciotomy and intrathecal baclofen therapy.

title: Spinal Cord Injury Medicine Fellowship
inst: University of Miami Miller School of Medicine / Jackson Health System
Summary: The UM/Jackson one-year ACGME-accredited SCI fellowship trains fellows across acute trauma, post-acute rehabilitation and translational research with the South Florida SCI Model System, the Miami Project to Cure Paralysis and the Miami VA SCI Unit.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship (Hershey)
inst: Penn State Health Milton S. Hershey Medical Center / Penn State College of Medicine
Department: Departments of Family and Community Medicine and Orthopaedics and Rehabilitation
Eligibility: Board-eligible or board-certified family medicine candidates who have completed (or are completing) an ACGME-accredited family medicine residency and are ABFM certified or scheduled to sit boards before the start; significant commitment to an academic sports medicine career
Accreditation: Fully accredited by the ACGME; graduates eligible for the CAQ in Sports Medicine
Application method: ERAS with three letters (one from a sports medicine physician); participates in the NRMP
Funding: Stipend and benefits at the appropriate PGY level; AMSSM membership and meeting support
Summary: Penn State Hershey's one-year ACGME-accredited primary care sports medicine fellowship covers sports, occupational medicine, cardiac rehabilitation and fitness, with Hershey Bears, Harrisburg Senators, Division II/III college and high school coverage.

title: Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship (State College)
inst: Penn State Health (State College) / Penn State College of Medicine
Department: Department of Family and Community Medicine
Eligibility: Completed residency in family medicine or PM&R from an ACGME-accredited programme before the start; three letters (one from residency PD), signed AMSSM Code of Ethics, USMLE/COMLEX scores
Summary: Penn State Health's State College primary care sports medicine fellowship admits one fellow per year, with a weekly family medicine continuity clinic, teaching, and diagnostic and interventional MSK ultrasound.

title: Brain Injury Fellowship
inst: Penn State Health Milton S. Hershey Medical Center / Penn State Health Rehabilitation Hospital
Eligibility: Graduates of an ACGME-accredited residency in PM&R, neurology or psychiatry
Accreditation: ACGME-accredited; satisfies eligibility for the Brain Injury Medicine subspecialty examination
Application method: ERAS only; participates in the NRMP and positions are not filled outside the match
Summary: Penn State's 12-month ACGME-accredited brain injury fellowship covers acute trauma, acute and post-acute rehabilitation across mild to severe acquired brain injury at Penn State Health Rehabilitation Hospital and Hershey Medical Center.

title: Sports Medicine Fellowship
inst: Cone Health (Moses H. Cone Memorial Hospital)
Department: Cone Health Family Medicine Residency (with UNC Chapel Hill and Piedmont AHEC)
Eligibility: Recent graduates of family medicine or med-peds residencies; emergency, internal medicine, pediatrics and PM&R graduates considered with strong ambulatory and sports medicine experience
Accreditation: Fully accredited by the ACGME (programme began 1992)
Application method: NRMP Primary Care Sports Medicine Fellowship Match
Summary: Cone Health's sports medicine fellowship, among the first fully ACGME-accredited (since 1992), makes fellows primary team physicians for a local college and high school with at least 2,000 sports-injury encounters a year.
